=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:272-288 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The activation_open_prs_json jq filter passes open PRs from any author (fork or outside contributors) into the model context without an author or trust check.
  WHY: This is inconsistent with the script's trust model at lines 405 and 596 (github-actions[bot] or OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR). A crafted PR can lead the model to tag a gap `open_pr` and suppress the ai:activation-fix:v1 issue. Severity was NIT for sonnet, gemini, minimax and glm, and MAJOR for the related openai finding below; the highest is used here only for the shared 272-288 trust-boundary root cause, and the openai entry is kept separate.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:278-280, 163, 604 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: An `open_pr` tag is accepted after checking only that the PR number appears in the list, with no check that the PR actually changes files relevant to the gap.
  WHY: A listed PR can claim to address a gap without containing the fix. If the model tags it, the gap is omitted from the activation-fix issue and has no pipeline follow-up. Source severity was MAJOR.
- prompts/mode-plan.txt:140-146 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The rule "When that work is already on the planning ref, plan no edits." names no STATUS to emit, unlike the adjacent open-PR case, which mandates STATUS: NOT_CLEAR.
  WHY: A planner could emit STATUS: CLEAR with no edits, which is auto-approved and leads to an empty or no-op implement run. Severity disagreement: NIT for sonnet, gemini and openai, MAJOR for minimax; the highest is used.
- prompts/_templates/mode-plan.txt:133-139 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The template twin has the same rule with no STATUS directive for the "already on the planning ref" case (openai cites line 136).
  WHY: The planner can emit a plan that proceeds toward approval despite there being no work to implement.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:506-512 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The open_pull_requests context merge passes the whole payload as one jq --argjson argument, which can exceed the per-argument limit (E2BIG) with 50 large PR bodies. The fail-open branch at lines 510-511 then drops the list with no ::warning::.
  WHY: Duplicate-PR prevention silently stops working with no diagnostic.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: plan.yml already sends a BLOCKER with no questions to `ai:blocked`, and the unblock judge's `wait` / `pr_on_branch` hold resumes the issue once that PR is on `main` (PR description, plan-prompt deliverable)
  expected_change_site: prompts/mode-plan.txt and prompts/_templates/mode-plan.txt
  confidence=2
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: prompts/mode-plan.txt:143 says "When that work is already on the planning ref, plan no edits." with no required STATUS or self-check directive, while the adjacent open-PR case mandates STATUS: NOT_CLEAR
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:272-288 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The jq filter in activation_open_prs_json selects every open PR with no author check, unlike the trust model at lines 405 and 596.
  WHY: An outside PR's text can lead the model to set `open_pr`, leaving the gap out of the fix issue. The impact is limited, since the tag must be an integer from the list and the gap still appears in the verdict comment.
- prompts/mode-plan.txt:143 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: "When that work is already on the planning ref, plan no edits." names no STATUS, unlike the adjacent open-PR case.
  WHY: A planner could emit STATUS: CLEAR with no edits, but this does not make existing behavior worse.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- prompts/mode-plan.txt:140-146 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The rule for work already on the planning ref lacks a mandatory status directive.
  WHY: It may cause misclassification of plan status compared with the adjacent open-PR rule that mandates STATUS: NOT_CLEAR.
- prompts/_templates/mode-plan.txt:133-139 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The same rule in the template lacks a mandatory status directive.
  WHY: It may cause misclassification of plan status compared with the adjacent open-PR rule that mandates STATUS: NOT_CLEAR.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:272-288 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The jq filter for open_pull_requests retrieves titles, heads and bodies from all authors without a trust filter.
  WHY: Untrusted fork or external content enters the model context, which widens the trust boundary beyond the script's other trust gates.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:272-288 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The jq filter passes open PRs from any author into the model context, against the trust model at lines 405 and 596.
  WHY: A crafted PR title or body can make the model set `open_pr` and suppress the ai:activation-fix:v1 issue for that gap; the pipeline never re-checks this trust gate.
- prompts/mode-plan.txt:143 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The "already on the planning ref" case gives no STATUS directive, while the open-PR case says to emit PLAN_SELF_CHECK: BLOCKER and STATUS: NOT_CLEAR.
  WHY: A planner can emit STATUS: CLEAR with an empty plan, which is auto-approved. Implement then runs on an empty plan and ends BLOCKED or opens a no-content PR.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:278-280, 163, 604 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The script accepts an `open_pr` tag after checking only that the number appears in the list, with no check that the PR changes relevant files.
  WHY: A listed PR can claim to address a gap without containing the fix. If the model tags it, the gap is omitted from the activation-fix issue and has no follow-up.
- prompts/mode-plan.txt:143; mirrored in prompts/_templates/mode-plan.txt:136 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The no-edit rule does not specify the required self-check or STATUS.
  WHY: Without a required outcome for this case, the planner can emit a plan that proceeds toward approval despite there being no work to implement.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:272-288 (jq select on line 278) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The open-PR listing applies no author gate, which is inconsistent with the trust model at scripts/activation_verify.sh:596.
  WHY: A fork PR body that names a real gap can steer the model into tagging it `open_pr`, so the fix issue is never opened and nothing implements the gap.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:506-512 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The merge passes the whole open_pull_requests payload as one jq --argjson argument, which can exceed the per-argument limit (E2BIG) with 50 large PR bodies. The fail-open branch at lines 510-511 then drops the list with no ::warning::.

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "plan.yml already sends a BLOCKER with no questions to `ai:blocked`, and the unblock judge's `wait` / `pr_on_branch` hold resumes the issue once that PR is on `main`" (PR description, plan-prompt deliverable)
  Expected change site: prompts/mode-plan.txt and prompts/_templates/mode-plan.txt
  Evidence of absence: prompts/mode-plan.txt:143 carries no required STATUS or self-check directive for the "already on the planning ref" case. A planner following it literally can emit an edit-free plan with STATUS: CLEAR, which plan.yml auto-approves.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
